gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Model Y Standard lost the rear seat heaters along with the 8-inch rear screen. Seat-heat control is one of the factory rear screen's main jobs on the trims that have the screen, and an add-on screen in a Standard has no rear heaters to control.
standout_why: I compared against the cited owner's-manual 'Touchscreen' section, read through ManualsLib's copy of the 2025+ manual (result 16) because tesla.com returned HTTP 403 for results 1, 3, 4 and 5. I also compared against Not a Tesla App (result 18, 2026-06-05). The manual lists rear seat heaters as a rear-screen control but does not say which trims have the screen. The Not a Tesla App article covers only the 16-inch front screen across the base RWD/AWD, Premium and Performance trims and never mentions a rear screen. ChatGPT's answer said only that 'some Standard versions do not' have the screen and still listed seat heating as a feature. None of these pages says the Standard also has no rear seat heaters, and none says what that means for an add-on screen.
decides: The finding splits the pick by trim. On Premium and Performance (Juniper) the factory screen already handles rear climate, rear seat heat, front-passenger seat movement, streaming, games and two Bluetooth headphones. Those owners should skip add-on displays and add a tablet mount or the projector screen only for something bigger. On the Standard, an add-on rear display such as the Hansshow H86 for Juniper Standard brings back entertainment and, according to its maker (I could not open the page to re-check), rear climate control. It cannot bring back rear seat heating, because the car has no rear seat heaters. The table's 'plays' and 'controls' cells for Standard-fit screens should drop 'seat heat'.
